items.title: 13.9 Reactions of halides (X-) with concentrated sulfuric acid

source_refs.note: Topic 13.9, printed page 299. The printed '2HBr(s)', '8HI(s)' and '2SO2' are noted.

blocks.text: The halide ions react differently with concentrated sulfuric acid; the products and the nature of the reaction change down the group. With sodium fluoride, fumes of hydrogen fluoride are produced, NaF(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HF(g); HF is a weak reducing agent and does not react further. With sodium chloride, fumes of hydrogen chloride: NaCl(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HCl(g). With bromide, steamy fumes of hydrogen bromide and brown fumes of bromine are produced with the smell of sulfur dioxide, a redox reaction in which HBr reduces sulfuric acid to SO2 and is itself oxidised to bromine: NaBr + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HBr, then 2HBr + H2SO4 gives Br2 + SO2 + 2H2O. With sodium iodide, fumes of hydrogen iodide, purple fumes of iodine and the smell of H2S: HI is a strong reducing agent that reduces sulfuric acid to H2S and is oxidised to I2: NaI + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HI, then 8HI + H2SO4 gives 4I2 + H2S + 4H2O. The increasing reducing power of the halide ions from fluoride to iodide leads to the more complex reactions.
How does KI react with concentrated H2SO4, and what does this show about the reducing power of iodide?
